name: qm
pin_note: Moved from main@198faa2b to main@77024e79 (QM main on 2026-11-21, 2309 commits later) so the harness-evals crew holds one QM pin. At 77024e79 QM titles a session with claude-sonnet-5-5 (TITLE_MODEL_ID, src/agent/session-title-prompt.ts; utilityRoute in src/agent/agent-run.ts), so an Anthropic cell lists anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5 in utility_models beside anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5, its auxiliary model; without it the trial is HE-MODEL-001. tests/timer-turn-adapters.test.ts and tests/week-rig.test.ts are the keyless runs that show serve, timer turns and a restart working at this pin. Before that: moved from main@90e4ced7 to main@198faa2b (yc-software/qm#3206, QM main on 2026-11-08, 17 commits later) so serve can register the world MCP server again: 198faa2b adds PRIVATE_NETWORK_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, and the runner gives core the world's origin there for every QM serve trial (runner/trial/trial.ts). Before that: moved from main@b6786d67 to main@90e4ced7 by the internal-task pilot amendment (docs/benchmarks/2026-11-06-qm-s1-edition/PREREGISTRATION.md, Amendments); the prose fields below were read at b6786d67 or 90e4ced7 unless they name another commit. A counted run keeps the pin its preregistration commit holds.
install: git init && git fetch --depth 1 <repo> 77024e79699565296bdde10974ae3d26fd393df8 (no release tag past v0.1.15; the build checks git rev-parse HEAD) && build as deploy/core/Dockerfile does at that commit (npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts, connector-sdk build); see Dockerfile
entry: /opt/harness/adapter.sh run | serve (task container in compose.yaml; HE_ENTRY selects it)
turn_command: node qm-api.mjs turn: POST /v1/turns {surface:'harness-eval', actor:{externalId:'U1'}, conversation:{kind:'dm', threadRef:<trial>}, text:<instruction.md>} signed with CORE_SIGNING_SECRET
inner_harness: pi, the only agent loop at this pin (src/agent/agent-run.ts). yc-software/qm#2768 removed the Claude harness and the HARNESS variable, and #2471 moved the mock harness to test support; core reads no HARNESS variable. HE_HARNESS_CONFIG selects only the probe settings (configs below)

model_particle.provider: custom provider particle (QM's own route for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, src/model/custom-providers.ts at the pin), registered by adapter.sh before the first turn
model_particle.model: custom/particle/<HE_MODEL_NAME> as core's PI_MODEL (prepare.sh QM_PI_MODEL); the request names the upstream id particle-1
model_particle.registration: PUT /v1/admin/custom-providers/particle as harness-admin: {name, protocol: openai, baseUrl: <HE_MODEL_BASE_URL>/v1, models: [{id: <HE_MODEL_NAME>, reasoning: true, contextWindow: 1048576, maxTokens: 128000}], apiKey: <HE_MODEL_API_KEY>, validate: false}; the request file holds the token and is deleted after the call; qm-custom-provider-register.json keeps the 200 (hasKey true, no key)
model_particle.core_environment: prepare.sh prints QM_PI_MODEL, and empty QM_MODEL_PROVIDER, QM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and QM_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL for a /particle URL only; compose.yaml reads them for core and falls back to the old values when unset. MODEL_PROVIDER=anthropic would make core refuse to start without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (src/deployment/secret-schema.ts)
model_particle.selected_when: HE_MODEL_BASE_URL ends in /particle (runner/trial/proxy.ts baseUrlFor); any other URL prints no override, so an Anthropic cell's core environment is unchanged (tests/particle-branch.test.ts)
model_particle.reasoning_setting: QM's default effort auto is medium for a non-Anthropic model (applyTurnEffort and defaultInteractiveThinkingLevel, src/agent/agent-run.ts and src/model/pi-models.ts), and pi-ai's openai-completions sends it as top-level reasoning_effort for a model with reasoning true; observed reasoning_effort medium on every request
model_particle.max_output_tokens_note: the custom model's maxTokens 128000, which pi-ai sends as max_completion_tokens (simple-options.js: maxTokens defaults to the model's); the cap the OpenAI cells run under. A custom model without maxTokens would default to 8192, too low for Particle's reasoning
model_particle.auxiliary_models: no Haiku call: auxiliaryModelFor finds no auxiliary model for provider particle, so title, detect, judge and screen calls name the cell model (src/model/pi-models.ts); the ack-emoji call is Anthropic-only and is skipped without an Anthropic key (pickAckEmoji, src/agent/agent-run.ts). Observed: one side call and one agent turn, both naming particle-1
model_particle.refusal_fallback: on a provider refusal or model_unavailable error Pi retries the turn on claude-opus-5 (REFUSAL_FALLBACK_MODEL_IDS, src/agent/agent-run.ts:833); core holds no Anthropic key on a Particle cell, so the retry reaches no model and the turn fails as a model error
model_particle.embeddings: none: QM's memory embedder is an org setting (embeddingModelId, src/resolution/config-store.ts), unset here
model_particle.observed_keyless: 2026-10-31, images harness-eval/qm:dev and qm-sandbox:dev built at the pin, the checkout's adapter mounted in the task container, one run turn through compose.yaml straight against tests/fixtures/particle/fake-particle.ts (the proxy's Particle route was not on main yet): exit 0, reply ok, two POST <base>/v1/chat/completions naming particle-1 (stream true, include_usage true, reasoning_effort medium, max_completion_tokens 128000; one side call with no tools, one agent turn with 13 tools), and an Anthropic trap URL on the fake was never called (tests/particle-branch.test.ts)
model_particle.error_mapping: qm-api.mjs maps a failed turn whose reason names the provider or model to exit 3, unchanged; Pi words every provider error that way, so on a Particle cell any provider 400 is exit 3, wider than plan decision 12. The runner applies decision 12 from the metering proxy record once that follow-up lands, and overrides this

model_openai.provider: openai, QM's built-in OpenAI provider (MODEL_PROVIDER=openai); no custom provider is registered
model_openai.model: <HE_MODEL_NAME> as core's PI_MODEL (compose.yaml), a model in QM's own registry: gpt-6.1-sol is src/model/model-registry.ts's row cloned from pi-ai's gpt-5.5 (context 1,050,000, maxTokens 128,000)
model_openai.base_url_env: OPENAI_BASE_URL (set from HE_MODEL_BASE_URL + /v1 by compose.openai.yaml); QM puts it in place of the base URL of every openai model, the cell model and the housekeeping model alike (resolveModel, src/model/pi-models.ts; src/model/provider-endpoints.ts)
model_openai.selected_when: the cell model's provider is openai (openai:<model>, so HE_MODEL_BASE_URL ends in /openai): runner/trial/docker.ts and harnesses/run-trial.sh merge compose.<provider>.yaml over compose.yaml when it exists. prepare.sh and adapter.sh have no OpenAI branch and print or register nothing more, so the per-trial token reaches core only as an environment variable, as on an Anthropic cell, and no request file holds it. An Anthropic or Particle cell loads no extra file (tests/qm-openai-branch.test.ts golden environments)
model_openai.core_environment: MODEL_PROVIDER openai (core then requires OPENAI_API_KEY, src/deployment/secret-schema.ts) and empty ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
model_openai.reasoning_setting: QM's default effort auto is medium for a non-Anthropic model (applyTurnEffort and defaultInteractiveThinkingLevel, src/agent/agent-run.ts and src/model/pi-models.ts), and pi-ai's openai-responses sends it as reasoning {effort: medium, summary: auto}; the proxy recorded reasoning_effort medium on all 1,318 requests of the qm-c4-told-live-2026-11 Sol cells (1,063 gpt-6.1-sol, 255 gpt-5.6-luna)
model_openai.max_output_tokens_note: the registry row's maxTokens 128000, which pi-ai sends as max_output_tokens (simple-options.js lowers it only when the context window is nearly full); the cap the OpenClaw Sol cells state and every shard's proxy runs at (--max-output-tokens 128000)
model_openai.auxiliary_models: gpt-5.6-luna, harness housekeeping, shipped default: auxiliaryModelFor gives the registry's auxiliary model for provider openai (src/model/pi-models.ts, model-registry.ts auxiliary true), so session titles and the other utility calls name gpt-5.6-luna through the same OPENAI_BASE_URL and token. It needs no Anthropic credential, so it is kept, metered and listed as openai:gpt-5.6-luna in the cell's utility_models; it is never an arm. The descriptive title model claude-sonnet-5-5 is used only by a user's regenerate-title request, which no trial sends
model_openai.fallback: QM's fallback model is an org setting at this pin (getPurposeRuntime fallback, src/wiring.ts), unset here, so a provider error is not retried on another model
model_openai.embeddings: none: QM's memory embedder is an org setting (embeddingModelId), unset here
model_openai.observed: counted at main@b6786d67 in qm-c4-told-live-2026-11 (cells qm-pi-sol-*-mu-v03-dev, docs/benchmarks/2026-11-03-qm-c4-told-live)
model_openai.observed_keyless: 2026-11-08, images harness-eval/qm:dev and qm-sandbox:dev built at 90e4ced7, the checkout's adapter mounted in the task container, one run turn through compose.yaml and compose.openai.yaml against tests/fixtures/openai-branch/fake-openai.ts: exit 0, reply ok, two streamed POST <base>/v1/responses with the dummy token, both with reasoning {effort: medium, summary: auto} and max_output_tokens 128000: one side call naming gpt-5.6-luna with no tools and one agent turn naming gpt-6.1-sol with 14 tools; core named no Anthropic model (tests/qm-openai-branch.test.ts)

state_paths: sandbox volume qm-home-<scope> (/root, the agent's workspace; removed by capture.sh)
mcp_config_path: QM's MCP server registry: PUT /v1/admin/mcp-servers/world at serve start (name world, url HE_WORLD_MCP_URL, auth bearer with HE_WORLD_MCP_TOKEN, credentialScope shared, readOnly false; approval, catalog and attestActor left unset, so QM's defaults apply: approval annotations, catalog off), as admin principal harness-admin (ADMIN_GRANTS in config/core.env); core probes tools/list before saving and keeps serverInfo.description, else the server instructions, as the server's about line (src/mcp/mcp-client.ts:94, src/api/routes/admin/mcp-servers.ts:229-231). From 198faa2b core dials the world only because the runner sets PRIVATE_NETWORK_ALLOWED_ORIGINS on core to the world's origin (http://host.docker.internal:<port>); without it publicFetch refuses the private address and the PUT answers 400 unreachable
sandbox_backend: local (one Docker container per scope via the host socket; image Dockerfile.sandbox). A scope has no sandbox until the agent creates one and sets it as the default (sandbox list, create, set_default; src/sandbox/sandbox-routing.ts:32-38, 71-75); execute with scope scratch runs on a per-turn container from the same image. The local backend still does not read QM_CORE_CONTAINER at b6786d67 (localSandboxEnv, src/config.ts:305-313; the QM_CORE_CONTAINER line at :288 is the AWS backend's), so core runs on the host network
multi_user_mode: QM scopes: personal:<slack user id> for a DM, channel:<id> for a channel; the actor is the requester's Slack user id on every turn
serve_turn_command: node qm-api.mjs turn: POST /v1/turns {surface:'harness-eval', actor:{externalId:<requester slack_user_id>, displayName}, conversation:{kind:'dm', threadRef:'dm:<member>'} | {kind:'channel', threadRef:'channel:<id>', channelRef:<id>, channelName}, text:<prompt>}

serve.session_key: conversation.threadRef dm:<member> | channel:<id>; scope personal:<actor> | channel:<id>. With TurnRequest.thread_ts set (a task turn with thread = "new"), :t<thread_ts> is appended, which opens a new QM session in the same scope
serve.shared_between_sessions: whatever QM shares across scopes under HARNESS_SHARING_POSTURE=isolated; not configured by the adapter
serve.exit_mapping: status ok, silent or pending_approval -> 0; request outlived the budget -> 124; refusalKind model_budget or a provider status in reason -> 3; else 2. A pending_approval turn keeps exit 0 and its TurnResult (pendingApprovals) is in <turn>.qm.json
serve.memory_snapshot: before every turn the adapter reads GET /v1/admin/memory/scopes and GET /v1/admin/memory?scope=<id> for each scope with memory, as harness-admin, into <turn>.memory.json (observation for the probe report; a failure is logged, never a turn failure)

gbrain_mcp: with HE_GBRAIN_MCP_URL and HE_GBRAIN_MCP_TOKEN set at serve start, PUT /v1/admin/mcp-servers/gbrain (name gbrain, url HE_GBRAIN_MCP_URL, auth bearer with HE_GBRAIN_MCP_TOKEN, credentialScope shared, readOnly false) as harness-admin, beside world; core probes tools/list before saving, so the registration's 2xx is the discovery proof (qm-gbrain-register.json). Unset, no registration happens

inner_harnesses.pi: QM's vendored pi-ai loop (src/agent/agent-run.ts, renamed from src/harness/pi-harness.ts); PI_MODEL from HE_MODEL_NAME (src/config.ts:1468); the configuration every earlier QM-Pi cell ran
inner_harnesses.claude: removed upstream at this pin (yc-software/qm#2768: 'remove the Claude harness and the harness concept; serve Claude subscriptions through Pi'). The adapter's claude and claude-probe configs are gone; earlier qm-claude results stay as they were published at v0.1.15
inner_harnesses.codex: none at this pin. Codex is only a ChatGPT-subscription model provider inside the Pi loop (src/agent/agent-run.ts CODEX_SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDER, src/model/codex-device-login.ts), not an inner harness

configs.pi: QM_HARNESS=pi; MEMORY_CAPTURE_QUIET_MS 180000 (shipped default, src/memory/strategies/per-turn.ts:9). Held-out cells
configs.pi-strict: pi-probe plus QM_PROBE_CONFIG=pi-strict: before the first turn the adapter PUTs {posture: "strict"} to /v1/admin/scopes/org:harness-eval/security-posture as harness-admin (qm-admin-security-posture.json holds the 2xx). strict also lifts the auto posture's private-network deny (security-posture.ts:17-21); the probe does not depend on that
configs.pi-command-deny: pi-probe plus QM_PROBE_CONFIG=pi-command-deny: PUTs a denylist command policy whose first rule denies \buname\b, followed by the shipped org floor rules (command-policy.ts:7-21, unchanged since v0.1.15), to /v1/admin/scopes/org:harness-eval/command-policy (first match wins, command-policy.ts:509-540; qm-admin-command-policy.json holds the 2xx)
configs.pi-memory-provider: QM_HARNESS=pi; MEMORY_CAPTURE_QUIET_MS 180000 (as pi) plus gbrain as QM's per-turn personal-scope memory provider (internal-task, harnesses/qm/memory-provider.ts): the runner gives core MEMORY_PROVIDER_CONFIG (provider gbrain at the world's /gbrain tap, read tool recall, queryArg question, maxCharsArg max_chars, timeoutMs 10000; routes default for every scope, then gbrain for personal with capture off and failOpen true) and a per-trial OAuth client pair (QM_GBRAIN_READ_CLIENT_ID, QM_GBRAIN_READ_CLIENT_SECRET) through the compose stack's environment, sets the gbrain upstream's provider block, and registers no gbrain MCP server (adapter.sh exits 2 if HE_GBRAIN_MCP_URL is set). prepare.sh exits 2 when any of the three variables is missing
configs.pi-skills-native: internal-task native arm: QM_HARNESS=pi with shipped settings on a skill-arm image (harness-eval.skill-arm catalog; scripts/skill-resolver/step0/qm/arms/Dockerfile.arms) whose core reads the 351-skill catalog as DEPLOYMENT_LAYER=/opt/catalog-layer. Before the turn adapter.sh records the org's installed skills (qm-skills-listed.json) and calls the resolver with --shadow on instruction.md, the member's own request (harnesses/qm/skill-resolver.mjs, the four push harnesses' command line and input): it logs one status line (skill-resolver/status.ndjson) and injects nothing. run entry only
configs.pi-skills-push: internal-task "emulated hook" arm: pi-skills-native's image and listing, but the resolver runs without --shadow and adapter.sh prepends its block, then one blank line, to the turn text (QM has no per-turn context hook at the pin). A result other than OK (an empty block, no_skill, a spent budget, an error) leaves the text unchanged. run entry only
configs.pi-skills-pull: internal-task "pull via sandbox tool (QM refuses private-address MCP)" arm: a skill-arm image (harness-eval.skill-arm catalog-pull) with the catalog and the resolve-skills deployment-layer tool, and the arm's sandbox image (QM_SANDBOX_IMAGE, default harness-eval/qm-sandbox:harn52-arm-pull, printed by prepare.sh) with the shim, gbrain and its index. After the turn adapter.sh reads the stored session and writes one status line per resolve-skills call the model made. run entry only
configs.pi-skills-none: internal-task no-catalog arm: a skill-arm image (harness-eval.skill-arm no-catalog) with no DEPLOYMENT_LAYER, SKILLS_SEED_DIR=/opt/no-such-skills (missing, so QM installs no seed skills) and PLUGIN_SKILLS_DIRS=false; adapter.sh records what QM still installs (qm-skills-listed.json). run entry only
configs.mapping: harnesses/qm/prepare.sh maps HE_HARNESS_CONFIG to QM_HARNESS (always pi; a label), QM_MEMORY_CAPTURE_QUIET_MS and QM_PROBE_CONFIG as NAME=value lines compose interpolates; the pi-skills-* configs also check the images' harness-eval.skill-arm label; an unknown value (claude and claude-probe included since b6786d67) exits 2

memory_capture_quiet_ms: 5000 in probe configs, 180000 (shipped) otherwise. Deviation, probe cells only: QM captures memory after a quiet period following a turn; at 180 s nothing is captured before a probe's next turn arrives, so the probe cells shorten it and their task turns wait 20 s. The held-out cells keep the shipped value
capture: capture.sh copies and removes every qm.sandbox container of org harness-eval (manifest qm-sandboxes.json with sha256), then starts pg under COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME and writes pg_dump of database qm to logs/qm-db.sql.gz (items, tool_calls, llm_prompt_envelopes, memory). The dump holds per-trial tokens and is never committed
org_scope: org:harness-eval (ORG_ID=harness-eval in config/core.env; orgScope() at src/config.ts:884)
mcp_exposure: At this pin MCP tools are not sent with their schemas. A server registered without catalog is listed in a ## Connectors note of at most about 2,000 tokens (one line per server with its about line cut to 120 characters, then one line per tool while the budget lasts) and the model reaches its tools through tool_search and mcp_call (src/agent/deferred-tools.ts:19-24, 66-132; src/agent/agent-tools.ts:3790-3830). A tool needs approval only when the server sets approval all, or under the default annotations policy when the tool declares destructiveHint true and not readOnlyHint (src/mcp/mcp-tool-service.ts:37-44). On a read-only turn QM hides tools the registration does not mark readOnly (src/agent/deferred-tools.ts:12-17)
